neighbours.label: the end of a proper name used as a brand or business name (Impact Cater|ing, Cupid's Cronies), as opposed to the + pole's possessive of a common noun
fire: All lunches at the fair are provided by Riverside Catering this year.
The cheapest site to join is Cupid's Corner, which charges nothing at first.
We ordered the cake from Martha's Bakeshop on the high street.
The event is sponsored by Greenleaf Landscaping and two local banks.
Tickets are sold only through Harper's Travel in the old arcade.
The repairs were done by Summit Roofing within a week.
Grandma still buys her yarn at Molly's Knits downtown.
The wedding flowers came from Bloom Florists near the station.
quiet: All lunches at the fair are provided by the school's kitchen this year.
The cheapest option is the club's basic plan, which charges nothing at first.
We ordered the cake from the village's only bakery on the high street.
The event is sponsored by the city's council and two local banks.
Tickets are sold only through the theatre's box office in the arcade.
The repairs were done by the building's owner within a week.
Grandma still buys her yarn at the town's market on Saturdays.
The wedding flowers came from the station's small garden.

notes: card flags broad (1.1%). Top examples mix brand names (Impact Catering, Cupid's), code attributes and nouns; the + pole is possessive 's after common nouns (the country's, the novel's). Near misses use common-noun possessives.
